verdicts.reason: All rules hold: a jq schema exit enforces one frame, one subject, and a numeric score; status is assisted as the brief rates it; an unscored result is accepted; checkRunnable false is honest because the scorer is absent.
A3 fails: the cmp determinism check and the one-frame count enforce 'that frame only', but nothing checks the brief's 'match the brief at that t' element.

All rules hold: a printed changed-frames count plus a numeric rescore comparison is program-readable and covers worst-frame-only, rescore, and the full-render wait; below threshold is a valid result; status is assisted and checkRunnable false is honest.

A3 fails: the manifest jq has no import field, so it cannot enforce 'check one animation before import'; clips length 1 only counts clips and does not show that one animation played; it also contradicts its own claim that a partial-stage manifest is valid, because the exact stages equality would fail it.

A1 fails: nothing defines which files belong to each change class, and terrain, light, character, and interaction edits often land in the same scene file, so git diff --name-only cannot show that only one change class was touched.

All rules hold: a pre-edit path:line quote of the named system and a git diff limited to those files are program-readable; the path walk is reported as not run because the connector is absent, which counts as a valid result; status is assisted and checkRunnable false is honest.
